q: How many distinct payment-related provisions does the Manner of Payment section (Sec. 12.5) set out for Design-Build Services?
o: Two
Six
Four
Three
n: Sec. 12.5 sets out four provisions: (12.5.1) progress billing and pro-rated RPF on discontinuance, (12.5.2) Client payment of labor/materials and the revolving fund, (12.5.3) Client payment of permits/licenses/incidentals, and (12.5.4) Owner-approved appointment and Owner-paid salaries of superintendent/purchasing agent/timekeeper/property clerk. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.1–12.5.4)

q: An Owner is deciding between the two Design-Build structures for a project with a PCC of ₱60,000,000, purely comparing the Recommended Professional Fee each would cost. Which structure works out cheaper for the Owner, and by how much?
o: Design-Build by Administration is cheaper, by ₱6,000,000
Design-Build on a GMC basis is cheaper, by ₱1,800,000
Design-Build by Administration is cheaper, by ₱1,800,000
Both structures cost exactly the same
n: By Administration: 7% × ₱60,000,000 = ₱4,200,000. On a GMC basis: 10% × ₱60,000,000 = ₱6,000,000. ₱6,000,000 − ₱4,200,000 = ₱1,800,000 cheaper under Administration — though the GMC basis trades that higher RPF for the Owner's cost-overrun protection of a guaranteed ceiling. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.4.1–12.4.2)

q: Which listed method of compensation has the Architect's professional fee embedded directly within the project's fee ceiling, rather than billed as a separate item?
o: Built into the Guaranteed Maximum Cost
Professional Fee plus Expenses
Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense
Per Diem, Honorarium plus Reimbursable Expenses
n: 'Built into the Guaranteed Maximum Cost' is the method where the Architect's fee is not itemized separately but is already incorporated within the agreed GMC figure. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.3.7)

q: While handling both design and construction of a Design-Build project, an Architect discovers a personal business interest in the general contracting firm involved. What does Sec. 12 require the Architect to do?
o: Immediately resign from the project without informing the Client of the reason
Disclose the business investment or venture whenever required, per the Architects Credo pledge, so it does not compromise the Client's interest or the Architect's impartial judgment
Transfer the interest to a relative and continue without disclosure
Say nothing, since business interests are outside the scope of the SPP
n: Sec. 12's citation of the Architects Credo requires disclosure, whenever required, of any business investment or venture that may create a conflict of interest, so it neither compromises the Client's legitimate interest nor interferes with the Architect's duty of impartial judgment. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.2.2.2)

q: Using the Sec. 12.4.2 rate, how much is the Architect's Design-Build RPF for this project?
scenario: A different project under Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost (GMC) basis has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱80,000,000. The GMC ceiling agreed upon with the Owner is ₱88,000,000, with the Architect's RPF built directly into that ceiling.

q: Under Sec. 12's discussion of the Manner of Providing Services, when an Architect becomes involved in construction (including of his/her own design) through an arrangement other than the standard ones, which SPP issuances govern the Architect's continued separate professional identity, prerogatives, and integrity?
o: SPP Document 208 and SPP Document 209
Only the Architects Credo, with no reference to any other SPP document
SPP Document 200 (Code of Ethical Conduct) and SPP Document 202
SPP Document 203 and SPP Document 204
n: The Architect must retain a separate, distinct professional identity, prerogatives, and integrity as an Architect, remaining subject to the standards and tenets of SPP Document 200 (the Code of Ethical Conduct) and SPP Document 202. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.2.2.1)

q: On a Design-Build project, who is responsible for paying the cost of building permits, licenses, and other incidentals to the work?
o: The Owner/Client
Split equally between Architect and Owner
The General Contractor exclusively
The Architect, deductible from the RPF
n: Sec. 12.5.3 states the Owner/Client shall pay for the cost of all permits, licenses, and other incidentals to the work. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.3)

q: What is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for an Architect performing Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost (GMC) basis?
o: 6% of the PCC only
12% of the PCC, inclusive of Regular Design Services
7% of the PCC, exclusive of the Architect's Fee for Regular Design Services
10% of the PCC, or already built into the GMC, exclusive of the Architect's Fee for Regular Design Services
n: Sec. 12.4.2 sets the RPF for Design-Build Services on a GMC basis at 10% of the PCC, or already built into the Guaranteed Maximum Cost, exclusive of the Architect's Fee for Regular Design Services. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.4.2)

q: Regardless of which compensation method is chosen under Sec. 12.3, which party ultimately bears the cost of labor, materials, permits, licenses, and other incidentals on a Design-Build project?
o: The Architect
The Owner/Client
It is always split 50/50 between Architect and Owner
The general contractor's bonding company
n: Sec. 12.5 consistently places these costs on the Owner/Client: the Client pays all labor and material costs directly, and the Owner/Client pays for all permits, licenses, and other incidentals — independent of which compensation method under Sec. 12.3 is used. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.2–12.5.3)

q: An Architect is engaged for Design-Build Services by Administration on a project with a PCC of ₱40,000,000. Before completion, the Owner discontinues the project once construction has reached 65% completion. Per Sec. 12.5.1, how much pro-rated RPF is owed to the Architect?
n: Total RPF = 7% × ₱40,000,000 = ₱2,800,000. Since work stopped at 65% completion, the pro-rated RPF component owed is 65% × ₱2,800,000 = ₱1,820,000, payable by the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.1)

q: Which method of compensation under Sec. 12.3 combines a fixed daily rate and an honorarium together with reimbursement of expenses?
o: Mixed Methods of Compensation
Percentage of PCC
Per Diem, Honorarium plus Reimbursable Expenses
Lump Sum or Fixed Fee
n: This method pays the Architect a per diem rate plus an honorarium, on top of reimbursement of expenses incurred. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.3.5)

q: As a whole, what does Sec. 12 of SPP Doc. 207 govern?
o: The tenets of the Code of Ethical Conduct for all architects
The qualifications of a Foreign Architect practicing in the Philippines
The classification, compensation methods, recommended fees, and manner of payment for an Architect performing Design-Build Services
The composition and duties of an Architectural Design Competition's Secretariat
n: Sec. 12 (SPP Doc. 207) sets out the two types of Design-Build Services, their methods of compensation, the recommended professional fees, and the manner of payment governing the arrangement. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12)

q: Since the RPF here is built into the ₱88,000,000 GMC ceiling, how much of that ceiling is left for actual construction cost?
n: ₱88,000,000 (GMC ceiling) − ₱8,000,000 (RPF built in) = ₱80,000,000, which matches the stated PCC — confirming the GMC ceiling equals PCC plus the built-in RPF. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.4.2)
scenario: A different project under Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost (GMC) basis has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱80,000,000. The GMC ceiling agreed upon with the Owner is ₱88,000,000, with the Architect's RPF built directly into that ceiling.

q: Per the Architects Credo pledge invoked in Sec. 12, what must an Architect disclose whenever required?
o: The names of all other clients served that year
The Architect's personal annual income
The Architect's method of compensation on unrelated projects
Any business investment or venture that may tend to create a conflict of interest
n: Whatever mode the Architect adopts to be involved in construction, he/she must adhere to the Architects Credo pledge to disclose, whenever required, any business investment or venture that may tend to create a conflict of interest. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.2.2.2)

q: An Architect on a Design-Build project wants to appoint a construction superintendent, purchasing agent, timekeeper, and property clerk. What does Sec. 12.5 require regarding this appointment and who pays their salaries?
o: Only the Owner/Client may appoint such personnel; the Architect has no role
The Architect may appoint them freely, and their salaries are deducted from the Architect's Fee
Their salaries are shared equally between the Architect and the Owner/Client
The appointment is subject to the Owner/Client's approval, and their salaries are paid by the Owner/Client and are not deductible from the Architect's Fee
n: Sec. 12.5.4 provides the Architect may appoint such personnel subject to the Owner/Client's approval, with salaries paid by the Owner/Client and not deductible from the Architect's Fee under the SPP. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.4)

q: In Sec. 12.4, both the 7% (by Administration) and 10% (GMC) Recommended Professional Fees are described as 'exclusive of the Architect's Fee for the Regular Design Services.' What does this mean in practice?
o: Regular Design Services become free once a Design-Build fee is charged
The Owner may choose to pay either the Design-Build fee or the Regular Design Services fee, but never both
The 7%/10% Design-Build fee is charged in addition to, and separate from, whatever fee the Architect is owed for the Regular Design Services
The 7%/10% figure already contains the Regular Design Services fee, so no additional billing is allowed
n: 'Exclusive of' means the Design-Build RPF (7% or 10% of PCC) does not include compensation for Regular Design Services; that fee is charged and paid on top of the Design-Build fee. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.4.1–12.4.2)

q: Which statement correctly summarizes Sec. 12's safeguard over money that passes through the Architect's hands during a Design-Build project's construction?
o: All project funds must bypass the Architect entirely and go directly to the general contractor
The Architect keeps sole, unaudited control over any funds advanced by the Client
The Architect never advances personal funds for the work; any revolving fund entrusted for expenditures is accounted for and subject to periodic Client audit
The Architect is expected to finance construction costs personally and recover them later with interest
n: Sec. 12.5.2 makes clear the Architect does not advance money for the work, and any revolving fund given beforehand is accounted for and subject to periodic auditing by the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.2)

q: A Design-Build engagement on a GMC basis has a PCC of ₱90,000,000. Construction is suspended after reaching 80% completion. Per Sec. 12.5.1, how much pro-rated RPF is owed to the Architect?
n: Total RPF = 10% × ₱90,000,000 = ₱9,000,000. At 80% completion when suspended, the pro-rated component is 80% × ₱9,000,000 = ₱7,200,000, payable by the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.1)

q: What does 'Mixed Methods of Compensation,' as listed under Sec. 12.3, refer to?
o: Splitting the Architect's fee evenly among several architects on the team
Combining two or more of the recognized compensation methods for a single Design-Build engagement
A method exclusive to government-funded Design-Build projects
Paying the Architect only in non-monetary consideration
n: Mixed Methods of Compensation is the option of blending more than one of the other listed compensation methods within one Design-Build engagement. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.3.6)

q: How do Design-Build Services by Administration and on a GMC basis generally differ in their fee structure and the risk each places on the Architect?
o: By Administration guarantees a maximum construction cost, while the GMC basis has no ceiling at all
Both carry an identical 7% RPF and an identical guaranteed cost ceiling
The GMC basis always costs the Owner less than Administration, regardless of PCC
By Administration carries a lower RPF (7% of PCC) without a fixed cost ceiling, while the GMC basis carries a higher RPF (10% of PCC) tied to the Architect guaranteeing a maximum construction cost
n: Design-Build by Administration is compensated at the lower 7% RPF without the Architect guaranteeing a cost ceiling, whereas the GMC basis carries the higher 10% RPF (or fee built into the GMC) because the Architect is tied to a guaranteed maximum construction cost. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.1–12.4.2)

q: An Architect handles Design-Build Services by Administration for a mixed-use development with a PCC of ₱25,000,000. Applying Sec. 12.4.1, what is the Architect's Recommended Professional Fee?
What is the purpose of the conflict-of-interest disclosure required by the Architects Credo, as cited in Sec. 12?
o: To ensure the conflict neither compromises the legitimate interest of the Client nor interferes with the Architect's duty to render impartial judgment
To transfer legal liability for the project entirely to the Client
To automatically disqualify the Architect from the project
To allow the Architect to charge an additional disclosure fee
n: Disclosure exists so that any potential conflict does not compromise the Client's legitimate interest and does not interfere with the Architect's duty to render impartial judgment. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.2.2.2)

q: How is the Architect supposed to bill for the Design-Build professional fee as the project proceeds?
o: Billing is at the sole discretion of the general contractor, not the Architect
The fee may only be billed once, upon full completion of construction
The Architect may bill and be paid for progress payments during construction, proportional to the percentage of progress of completion of the construction work
The entire fee must be paid upfront before construction begins
n: Sec. 12.5.1 states the manner of payment follows the progress of construction, with the Architect billing progress payments proportional to the percentage of completion. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.1)

q: Based on the Recommended Professional Fee under Sec. 12.4.1, how much is the Architect's Design-Build RPF for this project?
scenario: An Architect is engaged to provide Design-Build Services by Administration for a project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱50,000,000. The Owner also separately engages the same Architect for Regular Design Services, billed as a distinct ₱2,000,000 fee.

q: How many types of Design-Build Services are recognized under SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12, and what are they?
o: Two: Comprehensive Design-Build and Specialized Design-Build
Two: Design-Build Services by Administration, and Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost (GMC) basis
One: Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost basis only
Three: by Administration, on a GMC basis, and on a Lump Sum basis
n: Sec. 12 recognizes exactly two types of Design-Build Services: Design-Build Services by Administration (Sec. 12.1) and Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost basis (Sec. 12.2). (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.1–12.2)

q: Midway through a Design-Build project, the Architect proposes to personally advance cash out of pocket to buy construction materials so work is not delayed. Is this consistent with Sec. 12.5?
o: Yes, but only up to 10% of the PCC
No — only the Regular Design Services fee may ever be advanced by the Architect
Yes — the Architect is required to advance funds and later bill the Client with interest
No — the Architect does not advance money for expenditures connected with the work; the Client directly pays all costs of labor and materials
n: Sec. 12.5.2 states the Client directly pays all costs for labor and materials, and the Architect does not advance any money for expenditures connected with the work. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.2)

q: How many distinct methods of compensation for Design-Build Services are enumerated under Sec. 12.3?
o: Four
Five
Nine
Seven
n: Sec. 12.3 enumerates seven methods: Percentage of PCC; Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense; Professional Fee plus Expenses; Lump Sum or Fixed Fee; Per Diem, Honorarium plus Reimbursable Expenses; Mixed Methods; and Built into the Guaranteed Maximum Cost. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.3.1–12.3.7)

q: Why is the Recommended Professional Fee higher for Design-Build Services on a GMC basis (10%) than for Design-Build Services by Administration (7%)?
o: Because the GMC rate already includes the Regular Design Services fee while the Administration rate does not
Because guaranteeing a maximum construction cost places greater responsibility and risk on the Architect, warranting a higher fee
Because GMC projects always involve larger PCC values than Administration projects
There is no real difference — both rates apply to the same risk profile
n: The GMC basis obliges the Architect to commit to a guaranteed maximum construction cost, a heavier undertaking than the open Administration arrangement, which is reflected in the higher 10% RPF versus 7%. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.4.1–12.4.2)

q: A Design-Build engagement on a GMC basis covers an industrial facility with a PCC of ₱120,000,000. Applying Sec. 12.4.2, what is the Architect's Recommended Professional Fee?
Which of the following is NOT one of the methods of compensation for Design-Build Services listed under Sec. 12.3?
o: Lump Sum or Fixed Fee
Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee
Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense
Percentage of Project Construction Cost (PCC)
n: Sec. 12.3 lists seven methods: Percentage of PCC, Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense, Professional Fee plus Expenses, Lump Sum or Fixed Fee, Per Diem/Honorarium plus Reimbursable Expenses, Mixed Methods, and Built into the Guaranteed Maximum Cost. 'Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee' as worded is not one of the seven. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.3)

q: A Design-Build project is discontinued before construction is finished. What happens to the Architect's Recommended Professional Fee for the unfinished portion?
o: The full RPF for 100% completion is still owed regardless of actual progress
The Architect must return all RPF already received
The Architect forfeits the entire RPF since the work was not completed
The pro-rated RPF component is paid to the Architect by the Client
n: Sec. 12.5.1 specifies that should the work not be completed, the pro-rated RPF component shall be paid to the Architect by the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.1)

q: Given the Design-Build RPF and the separate Regular Design Services fee, what is the Architect's total professional fee from the Owner for this engagement?
n: Because the Design-Build RPF is exclusive of the Regular Design Services fee, the two are added: ₱3,500,000 + ₱2,000,000 = ₱5,500,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.4.1)
scenario: An Architect is engaged to provide Design-Build Services by Administration for a project with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of ₱50,000,000. The Owner also separately engages the same Architect for Regular Design Services, billed as a distinct ₱2,000,000 fee.

q: Which of the two Design-Build Service types is defined by the Architect committing to a fixed ceiling on construction cost?
o: Both types equally fix a cost ceiling
Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost (GMC) basis
Neither type involves a cost ceiling
Design-Build Services by Administration
n: The 'Guaranteed Maximum Cost' type ties the arrangement to a maximum/ceiling construction cost, distinguishing it from Design-Build by Administration, which does not carry that guaranteed ceiling. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.2)

q: At the start of a Design-Build engagement, the Owner sets up a fund that the Architect draws from for site-related expenditures, which the Owner periodically reviews and audits. Is this practice proper under Sec. 12.5?
o: Yes — this is the revolving fund practice, given to the Architect beforehand and subject to periodic auditing by the Client
Yes, but only if the Architect keeps the audit results confidential from the Owner
No — all such funds must instead be held by a third-party bank in the Architect's name alone
No — the SPP prohibits any fund from being placed under the Architect's control
n: Sec. 12.5.2 provides that, generally, a revolving fund is given to the Architect beforehand and is accounted for and subject to periodic auditing by the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.5.2)

q: What is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for an Architect performing Design-Build Services by Administration?
o: 2% to 5% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC)
10% of the PCC, exclusive of the Architect's Fee for Regular Design Services
7% of the PCC, exclusive of the Architect's Fee for Regular Design Services
A flat fee regardless of PCC
n: Sec. 12.4.1 sets the RPF for Design-Build Services by Administration at 7% of the PCC, exclusive of the Architect's Fee for Regular Design Services. (Source: SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.4.1)
